$comment: Contract Verification Aggregation SEP (draft) — an aggregator's Trusted Verifiers List. The Registry API draft left verifier discovery undefined; this is where the SEP defines it. Closed for a producer; a consumer validates with additionalProperties relaxed. No public_key: nothing is signed and this SEP defines no signature for 1.0, so a key field would have no producer and no consumer — the Design Rationale of the Contract Verification Results SEP carries the argument.
title: Trusted Verifiers List (Aggregation SEP 1.0)
description: The body of GET /v1/verifiers on an aggregator, listing every verifier it aggregates — paused and disabled members included. Without this route, the promise that an aggregator never silently omits a verifier is one a consumer cannot check. The list is authored by the aggregating operator; a verifier describes itself and does not admit itself to anyone's list, which is why no verifier-registration API exists.

schema.description: The document type. A list written before this SEP spells it `stellar-trusted-verifiers-list-v1`; a consumer accepts both.

verifiers.description: Every member, whatever its `status`. Filtering the list to the members currently being queried would make an omission and a pause indistinguishable from outside.

url.description: The verifier's result root, and **the identity of this entry**. Named `url` and not `cdn_root`: nothing here assumes a CDN, and a public contract should not. A verifier may call it a result root internally; what a reader needs is a URL. A list cannot hold two entries with the same one, because the same result root is the same verifier — which is why no entry needs an id.

manifest_url.description: Where this verifier serves a self-description of how it verifies — its build-image and source-mode policy, its retention, whom to contact. Optional: the document behind this URL is not defined by this SEP, and no field of this SEP is read out of it. Absent means the verifier publishes no such self-description; a consumer that finds one MUST treat it as advisory and MUST NOT derive any status, root or identity from it.

bulk_load_url.description: Where this verifier serves GET /v1/wasms, when it serves one. Absent means static files only: readable per Wasm hash, not enumerable — a conformance class, not a defect.

display_name.description: What the OPERATOR calls this verifier, for its own display. Optional, and not identity.

trust_tier.description: The operator's own assessment of this verifier. Free-form: the values are the operator's to choose and nothing interprets them across lists.

status.description: `paused` and `disabled` members stay listed. Removing a member from the document instead is how an aggregator silently omits a verifier.

id.description: OPTIONAL and implementation-local. An operator may key its own storage by a short id — ours does — but it means nothing outside the aggregator that minted it, and no other document refers to it. `url` is what identifies this entry.
